out.other_title: Do protocols that raise worst-case ASD resist rare catastrophic failures?
out.rationale: Sudhir et al. propose measuring worst-case rather than average-case ASD because superhuman oversight must prevent rare catastrophic actions. Brown-Cohen et al. state prover-estimator debate's guarantees are average-case only, the judge's payoff imperfectly tracks correctness, and formalising why average-case analysis is necessary is open; one is an empirical benchmark metric, the other a complexity-theoretic guarantee.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether average-case guarantees or metrics for oversight protocols are enough, given rare catastrophic failures

text: The authors state their results hold in an average-case rather than worst-case sense: they do not prove the judge can tell which debater is correct on every question, only that the payoffs incentivise debaters to converge to answering correctly, so the payoff is a random variable imperfectly correlated with correctness. They call formalising why such average-case analysis is necessary an open question, and ask whether there are lower bounds on B's circuit size for constant rho.
title: Limitation: average-case guarantees only; judge payoff imperfectly tracks correctness
